classification.difficultyReason: Read two rational-versus-linear comparisons across a pole, retaining equality endpoints and the excluded undefined value.

content.prompt: The graphs of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given.

spec.description: Qualitative decreasing two-branch curve and increasing line, with intersections labelled x=-6 and x=-1 and a vertical asymptote labelled x=-3.
spec.mathematics: Only the printed x-coordinates are numerical givens. Bézier control coordinates reproduce qualitative placement and do not define either function. The left intersection lies below the x-axis and the right intersection above it.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied curves, labels, intersection markers and guides remain visible; no solution intervals are added.

answer.worked:
The blue graph is on or above the red line for $x\leq-6$ and $-3<x\leq-1$. Include both intersection points because equality is allowed. Exclude $x=-3$, where $f$ is undefined.

$x\leq-6$ or $-3<x\leq-1$.

The blue graph is on or below the red line for $-6\leq x<-3$ and $x\geq-1$. Include both intersection points because equality is allowed. Exclude $x=-3$, where $f$ is undefined.

$-6\leq x<-3$ or $x\geq-1$.
